claims.text: Untreated, pre-exposure Q235 steel has a native surface oxide.
Q235 steel's room-temperature corrosion resistance is caused by a thin, continuous iron oxide layer.
The room-temperature iron oxide layer on Q235 steel is self-healing.
Exposure at 700–900 °C in molten salt destabilizes the protective oxide layer on Q235 steel.
Enhanced oxide dissolution contributes to high-temperature destabilization of the Q235 surface layer.
High-temperature microstructural or phase transformation contributes to destabilization of the Q235 surface layer.
The continuity, phase composition, porosity, and spallation of the iron oxide layer govern its protective behavior.
Elevated temperature accelerates the kinetics of oxide dissolution and phase transformation.
Oxide dissolution and phase transformation can produce porous or spalled oxide layers on Q235 steel.
Porous or spalled oxide layers permit further corrosion of Q235 steel.
High-temperature salt exposure will produce a less uniform and more porous oxide scale than room-temperature exposure.
High-temperature salt exposure will accelerate mass change and corrosion degradation relative to room-temperature exposure.
The oxide layer remains intact and protective when Q235 steel is maintained at room temperature in the same salt environment.
Substantial alloying with protective-layer-forming elements or applying an external coating may prevent the proposed mechanism.
Changes in salt composition may alter oxide dissolution kinetics and the resulting behavior.
Controlled annealing can mimic changes in oxide formation kinetics.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis assigns room-temperature protection to the proposed oxide mechanism, whereas the conditions state that the hypothesis is expected to hold at 700–900 °C and not at ambient conditions.

The design calls both the room-temperature and 800 °C media identical molten-salt environments, but it does not identify a salt chemistry that remains molten at room temperature. Thus the proposed temperature-only comparison is not operationally established.
